# workloadctl

> Declarative workload manager for Linux. A TOML file in `/etc/workloads.d/<name>/` becomes a dedicated unprivileged system user, systemd units, storage, secrets, networking and lifecycle, on two substrates: rootless-podman containers and KVM/QEMU virtual machines.

One workload, one unprivileged user (`_wl-<name>`). That uid is the selector everything keys on: egress policy matches it as `meta skuid`, storage is owned by it, the credential broker identifies callers by it, and software inside the workload cannot forge it. Both substrates share one TOML model and one command surface.

workloadctl is stdlib Python 3.14 plus a systemd generator, with no daemon of its own. It runs on ordinary Fedora 43+ and is bootc-ready. It requires moatery, which provides the egress inspector, the credential broker and the DNS responder.

- [Manual](docs/manual/README.md): eleven chapters, written to be read in order
  - [Concepts](docs/manual/01-concepts.md), [Installing](docs/manual/02-installing.md), [First workloads](docs/manual/03-first-workloads.md)
  - [Container workloads](docs/manual/04-containers.md), [VM workloads](docs/manual/05-vms.md)
  - [Networking and egress](docs/manual/06-networking.md): filtering, inspection, the credential broker
  - [Secrets](docs/manual/07-secrets.md), [Security and confinement](docs/manual/08-security.md)
  - [Operating](docs/manual/09-operating.md), [Troubleshooting](docs/manual/10-troubleshooting.md), [Reference](docs/manual/11-reference.md)
- [CLI reference](docs/cli.md): every command and flag, and the `--json` result shapes
- [Schema reference](docs/schema-reference.toml): every TOML key
- [Design decisions](docs/adr/README.md): ADRs 001 to 009

## Developer guide

- [Boot and generation](docs/dev/boot-and-generation.md): how a TOML becomes units, the run-file set, the CLI's layering
